title: Identifying Causal Transfers in Subsampled Process DAGs through Matrix-Root Fibers
banked_reason: D0.5 cold tier verdict: subfield; paper_score_ceiling 6.7 < 7.4 field floor; salvageable=false, with no bounded improvement directive.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived triangular root recursion, open singular-fiber witnesses, even-factor sign ambiguity, graph-local identification, and full-circle Wald inference. D0.5 found the archived note unclean: its derivative-separated-class nonemptiness iff omits oddness, it incorrectly names Q as real closed, and its equality-only adaptive branch is ballast. Bounded cleanup would not lift the structural subfield ceiling created by supplied order, known sampling factor, fixed dimension, recursion-defined separation, and no implementation/application.
tldr: Subsampling turns a fine-grid process DAG into a matrix-root problem, so a queried causal transfer is governed by the compatible fiber rather than by a selected numerical root.  For odd \(m\), seeding the queried edge and closing only under graph-supported remainder monomials gives an exact terminating dependency set: separation only there identifies the transfer and yields one uniformly calibrated Wald band for the entire curve in \(C(\mathbb T;\mathbb C)\).  Prespecified finite-frequency, directed-corridor, and globally separated Wald results remain explicit corollaries.  For even \(m\), the same-law sign obstruction continues to hold on the larger unrestricted stable Gaussian VAR(1) class with arbitrary positive-definite innovations.  Exact transfer-aware certification and branch-free confidence-region inversion cover singular and nonregular cases.
gap: Published subsampling results either invoke non-Gaussian shocks to identify the fine model, enumerate qualitative graph equivalence classes, or choose a numerical matrix-root branch. Published process-graph effect theory begins with fine-grid spectral information, and its Wald theory is local. No result decides a queried Gaussian transfer over the complete graph- and covariance-compatible root fiber.
fill: The project gives a parity-sharp graph recursion, a universal even-factor same-law obstruction, a total transfer-aware CAD fallback with exact witnesses, local Wald bands on an explicit regular class, and finite-sample branch-free inversion of a rationally rounded coarse-moment region.
